targeting.title: Ollama pull model manifest Error: What Each Message Means
targeting.metaTitle: Ollama pull model manifest Error Explained
targeting.metaDescription: Fix "Error: pull model manifest" in Ollama: what file does not exist, 412, ssh: no key found, no such host and Hugging Face 400 and 401 mean, with fixes.
targeting.excerpt: Every ending of the Ollama error "pull model manifest" explained from the 0.40.17 source and live registry tests: file does not exist, 412, ssh: no key found, network and certificate errors, and the Hugging Face 400, 401 and realm host replies, each with its fix.
targeting.keywords: ollama pull model manifest, error pull model manifest, ollama pull model manifest file does not exist, ollama pull model manifest 412, ollama pull model manifest 401, ollama pull model manifest ssh no key found, ollama pull model manifest no such host, ollama pull model manifest i/o timeout, ollama requires a newer version, ollama pull certificate signed by unknown authority, ollama realm host does not match original host, ollama pull error, ollama run pull model manifest file does not exist
targeting.summary: The text after the second colon is the real cause: file does not exist means the registry has no such name and tag, 412 means Ollama is too old for the model, and a line with Get https is a network problem|The manifest request is sent by the Ollama server and signed with its key file on every pull, so proxy, DNS and key fixes belong to the server process, not the terminal|Registry tests on 22 November 2026 showed 404 for wrong names and tags, 412 for gemma4 from an old version, and 400 or 401 replies from Hugging Face
targeting.author: Ali Rehman

research.notCovered: Autocomplete also suggests 'ollama create' and 'ollama save' with this error. In the 0.40.17 source only the pull handler starts a registry pull, and the create code does not call it, so the article makes no claim about ollama create. The 500 and EOF endings are listed in the keyword map but not explained, because I could not observe or source them.

competitors.gap: No page explains that the registry asks for a token on every pull and that the server signs it with a key file, which is why a damaged key stops public pulls. None covers the Hugging Face 400 and 401 replies, the realm host message or its 0.14.3 boundary, shows what the registries actually answer, or links any claim to the source code. No page offers one lookup table for all endings. binmage is stronger on 412 with a real install, so the 412 section here stays short and adds only the per-model test result.

validation.latestReleaseCheck: The GitHub releases API returned v0.40.17 as the latest release on 22 November 2026. Its tag commit is dated 21 November 2026 (UTC).
validation.releaseDateNote: The GitHub field published_at is the day a release entry first appeared as a pre-release, which can be up to 12 days before the final tag (seen for 0.10.0 and 0.40.0). This article therefore states no release dates.
validation.versionBoundaries: Binary search over the 274 stable release tags: the realm host check in server/auth.go is absent in 0.14.2 and present in 0.14.3; the manifest list Accept header in server/images.go is absent in 0.35.1 and present in 0.40.0; the 'pull model manifest' wrapper is already present in 0.1.20.

registryProbes.method: One manifest GET per case to the address Ollama builds, with the User-Agent and Accept header of the named Ollama version. When the registry asked for a token, the script completed the anonymous challenge described in server/auth.go and auth/auth.go with a throwaway ed25519 key held in memory, then repeated the GET. No blobs were downloaded; nothing was written to an .ollama folder.
registryProbes.supersededRuns: Files a, b, c and the first timestamped file used a manifest list Accept value that no Ollama version sends. With it, gemma4 'as 0.20.0' returned 412 and 'as 0.40.0' returned 200. All table rows were repeated with the header each version really sends: file f (current header, 13 cases) and file e (header of 0.35.1 and older, 9 cases). File d is the same run as f made before the script recorded the header. Files a, b, c, d and the timestamped file are kept for the record and are not used. File f also holds two combinations no real client sends (old version number with the new header); they are not used in the article.

validation.handsOn: curl -I against the registry and the two PowerShell Rename-Item commands were run on Windows 11 Pro build 26300 (the rename commands in a temporary test folder). Ollama was not installed or run. The Linux commands were not executed.
